title: Exact set partition

problem.name: Exact set partition
problem.statement_latex:
Given $U$, a nonempty-set family $\mathcal F\subseteq2^U$, and integer $k$, find $S_1,\ldots,S_k\in\mathcal F$ such that $U=S_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_k$. This is exact cover with a prescribed number of selected sets, and includes many clustering and assignment formulations.
The general comparison uses quantum QRAM time and classical subset-transform time; the explicit-family Boolean bounds count bit operations.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*((2+c)^{n/2})$ for eligible enumeration base $c<2$, Gaspers--Li partition framework.
quantum.headline_text: $O^*((2+c)^{n/2})$ for eligible enumeration base $c<2$, Gaspers–Li partition framework.
quantum.details_latex: Here $n=|U|$. A restricted-family branching algorithm must enumerate representative members in $O^*(c^{|X|})$ time while preserving a nonstraddling feasible partition. Theorems 5--6 refine the base for small $c$. The complexity includes preprocessing and assumes coherent access to its results; polynomial factors account for membership and feasibility tests.

classical.details_latex: For an explicit family of $m=\Theta(n)$ sets, selecting exactly one covering set per element and enforcing the chosen cardinality gives a stronger $O_\epsilon(2^{\epsilon n}\operatorname{poly}(n,m))$ bound for each fixed $\epsilon>0$. Long coverage clauses coexist with pairwise incompatibility constraints and a linear-size cardinality circuit. Long-clause shortening and bounded-width counting give the stated time. If the incidence count is linear, a linear-size encoding gives $\operatorname{poly}(n,m)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for an eligible large or implicit family, from amplitude amplification. Linear-size explicit families have a subexponential classical comparison.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomial active subset and cardinality registers are supplemented by exponential coherent memory. Large-instance fault-tolerant costs also include checking disjointness, membership and total coverage.
